title: Divergence checking does not maintain time-reversibility
author: howsiyu

comments.author: fehiepsi
comments.body: I guess when a divergence happens, we will ignore the trajectory and diagnose the model to find the issue. So I don't think we need to worry about the time-reversibility here.

comments.author: howsiyu
comments.body:
> when a divergence happens, we will ignore the trajectory and diagnose the model to find the issue. 

If that's the case, shouldn't numpyro stop immedately once it encounters a divergence post-warmup?

comments.author: martinjankowiak
comments.body: maybe numpyro should stop immediately because floating point errors violate time-reversibility ; )

comments.author: fehiepsi
comments.body: Closed because I don't think we should make an action here. Thanks for raising the issue, @howsiyu!
